title: Unemployment Benefit Claims — Claimant Handbook: Breaks in Certification and Reopening a Claim
content:
An active Unemployment Benefit Claims record becomes inactive when the number of consecutive uncertified weeks reaches the inactivity threshold. The weeks counted are the consecutive Saturday week ending dates after the latest certified week on the claim, through the latest week ending date whose certification window has closed, on which no certification is recorded.

## Reopening

1. An inactive claim is reopened at the claimant's request so that further weeks can be certified.
2. A claim may be reopened only on or before the benefit year end date of the claim. The reopen limit is counted in calendar days, with no grace days (0) after the benefit year end date, and a request on the benefit year end date itself is in time.
3. A claim is reopened only when its remaining balance is above zero; a claim with no remaining balance is not reopened.
4. When the claimant worked since the last certified week, the reopening is an additional claim and the new separation is recorded. An additional claim whose new separation is a voluntary quit or a discharge is placed on hold for a separation determination right after reopening where the program requires separation review.
5. The reopened claim keeps its original effective date, benefit year and balance, and weeks in the break that were never certified stay unpaid unless certified late with good cause.

The benefit year end date read is the one on the claim records.

## Both sides of the reopen limit

| Day of the request | Reopen limit |
|---|---|
| Before the benefit year end date | In time |
| On the benefit year end date | In time |
| The day after the benefit year end date | Too late |

## Questions answered

**Does a break keep the claim's balance?** Yes; the reopened claim keeps its original balance, effective date and benefit year.

**Is a reopening after intervening work handled differently?** It is an additional claim, and the new separation is recorded; a voluntary quit or discharge places the claim on hold for a separation determination where the program requires separation review.

### Hypothetical illustration

With an inactivity threshold of 2, a claimant who last certified the week ending on a given Saturday and certified neither of the next two weeks, both of whose windows have closed, has 2 consecutive uncertified weeks and the claim becomes inactive.
